summary: Herman Wirth was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Utrecht University (~1904–1908), held a post at the University of Bern (~1909–1914), and founded Ahnenerbe.

Hermann Beckh worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kiel University and earned his PhD at the University of Berlin (~1903–1907), later serving there as Privatdozent (~1908–1921) and at the Prussian State Library (~1916–1920).
Hermann Berger was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Helmut Hoffmann (~1950–1958) and took up a post at the University of Heidelberg in 1965.
Hermann Beythan worked in Indology and linguistics. Between ~1908 and 1914, he studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

Hermann Bonitz specialized in philosophy and linguistics. After studying at the universities of Leipzig (~1832–1834) and Berlin (~1834–1836), he held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (~1875–1888).

Indologist and linguist Hermann Brockhaus studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He held professorships at the University of Jena (1839) and the University of Leipzig (1848; 1872–1877), and founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Hermann Brunnhofer studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Zurich (PhD), as well as under Albrecht Weber (~1871–1875). His career included posts at Kuldīga Gymnasium, Oxford, Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek, the University of Saint Petersburg, and the University of Bern (1901–1914).
Hermann Camillo Kellner worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1865–1872) and served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Königliches Gymnasium Zwickau (~1876–1904).

Linguist and Indologist Hermann Collitz studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Halle under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He taught at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and held a chair at Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928).
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1878–1883) and served as professor of mathematics at the University of Giessen (~1902–1922).

Hermann Goetz studied at the University of Munich (~1920–1923) and under Jean Philippe Vogel (~1931–1936). He held posts at the Baroda Museum (1939–1953), National Gallery of Modern Art (~1953–1955), and University of Heidelberg (1961–1976).
Hermann Güntert worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1921–1923) and the University of Heidelberg (~1923–1945).

Hermann Günther Grassmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher (~1827–1830) and taught at the Friedrich-Wilhelms-Schule (~1842–1852) and the Marienstiftsgymnasium (1832–1834; 1852–1877) in Stettin.

Indologist and linguist Hermann Hirt studied at the University of Freiburg (~1884–1888) and the University of Leipzig (~1888–1891). He taught at Leipzig (1891–1912) before serving as professor at the University of Giessen (1912–1936).

Hermann Hunger works in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Vienna, Münster, and Heidelberg, and held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (~1968–1970), University of Chicago (~1970–1973), and University of Vienna (~1978–2007).

Hermann Jacobi worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, studying at Bonn, Berlin, and Calcutta under Albrecht Weber and Johann Gildemeister. He held professorships at Münster (1876–1885), Kiel (1885), and Bonn (1889–1922).

Historian and Indologist Hermann Kulke studied at Freiburg, Madras, and Heidelberg under Hermann Goetz. He served as professor of Indian history at the University of Heidelberg (1967–1988) and held the Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988–2003).

Hermann Oldenberg worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin, and held professorships at the University of Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889; 1898; rector 1906–1907), and the University of Göttingen (1908).

Linguist and Indologist Hermann Osthoff studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He worked at the University of Leipzig (~1875–1877) before becoming an Ordinarius at the University of Heidelberg in 1877.

Hermann Sauppe worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann (~1828–1832) and held positions at the University of Zurich (1833; 1838) and the University of Göttingen (professor from 1855).
